newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court fines sect members for Islamic dress.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court fines sect members for Islamic dress.

text.p: A Turkish court on Tuesday imposed nominal fines on more than 100 Islamist sect members for breaking a law on wearing religious clothes in public, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.

It said 125 members of the Aczimendi sect were fined 300,000 Turkish Lira ($2) each for refusing to change out of their black robes and turbans at an earlier trial, as demanded by Moslem Turkey's secular constitution.
The fines set by the Turkish penal code have not been revised for years and their value has been cut by inflation.
Turkey's military-dominated security council last month ordered the country's first Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to crack down on rising Islamist activism.
Among their demands was the enforcement of the Islamic dress ban, as well as action to close down Islamist sects and rein in illegal religious instruction classes.

The Aczimendis were earlier charged under the country's anti-terror law for anti-state activities following a rowdy religious ceremony last year. They would face between three to ten years in jail if found guilty under the law.
The Aczimendis, a small sect based in the eastern city of Elazig, dress in dark robes and turbans and carry long staffs.
